introduction: Today we celebrate the solemnity of Saints Peter and Paul, the two great apostles who gave their lives for Christ in Rome. Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and received the keys of the Kingdom. Paul, at the end of his life, says that he has fought the good fight and kept the faith. Let us pray for the Pope, successor of Peter, and for the whole Church built on the faith of the apostles.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord built his Church on the faith of the apostles. Let us pray to him for the whole Church.
intentions: For the Pope, successor of Saint Peter: that the Lord may strengthen him to confirm his brothers and sisters in faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
For bishops, priests and missionaries: that, like Saint Paul, they may proclaim the Gospel fully and fearlessly. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians in prison or persecuted for their faith: that the Lord may stand by them and strengthen them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the unity of all Christians: that we may be one in the faith handed down by the apostles. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may answer the question of Jesus with Peter's faith: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you gave your Church the witness of Saints Peter and Paul. By their prayers, keep us faithful to the teaching of the apostles and bring us to the crown of righteousness. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Who do you say that I am?
reflection.body:
Peter and Paul were very different men. Peter was a fisherman from Galilee who walked with Jesus for three years; Paul was a learned Pharisee who persecuted the Church before Christ called him on the road to Damascus. They even disagreed at times. Yet the Church honors them on the same day, because both gave their lives for Christ in Rome, and together they are pillars of the Church.

In the Gospel, Jesus asks his disciples a question that no one can answer for us: "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answers, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus tells him that this faith is a gift from the Father, and he gives Peter a new role: "you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it." He entrusts him with the keys of the Kingdom.

The first reading shows the Church praying for Peter in prison: "constant prayer was made by the assembly to God for him." An angel leads him out, and Peter says, "Now I truly know that the Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me."

Paul, near the end of his life, writes to Timothy: "I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith." He has not done it alone: "But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me."

Today we pray for the Pope, Peter's successor, as the first Christians prayed for Peter. And each of us must answer the question of Jesus personally. This week, ask yourself who Jesus is for you, and tell him in your own words. Then pray for the Pope by name.
